messages:
jenni (customer): Hey team — our web app started returning 403s from the POST /v1/generate endpoint around 09:12 UTC after we flipped the new UI. No code changes to our API keys. Dev environment works fine. Pls help, customers are hitting paywall in prod :grimacing:

alex (support): Sorry you're seeing that — can you paste the exact curl you used and the full response (headers + body)? Also send the account/org ID so we can look up entitlements.

jenni (customer): Sure. Org: org_9f3b. Repro steps: 1) Use production API key 2) POST to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 3) body {"prompt":"test"}. Response is below:

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Thu, 23 May 2024 09:12:04 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: r-3b9f2c

{"error":"Forbidden","message":"Access denied"}

alex (support): Thanks. That body is generic — could be auth or entitlement. Two quick checks: is the key definitely the prod key (starts with "rk_live_")? Any recent plan changes on your side? Also I asked internal to look at x-request-id r-3b9f2c.

jenni (customer): Yes prod key (rk_live_...). No plan changes we made. We did enable the new UI feature flag on our product dashboard at 08:58 UTC. Not sure if that matters.

maria (eng-platform): Looking at r-3b9f2c in logs: entitlement check failed downstream. We passed the request to feature-entitlements service which returned 403 with reason code ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED but the gateway strips reason and returns a generic 403 body.

alex (support): Ah — so it's not an API key auth failure but a plan/feature entitlement gate. The gateway returning a generic 403 is causing confusion (customers think key is bad).

sam (billing): We rolled out a billing tier change for a small customer cohort this morning to turn on the new UI as part of a seat migration migration-job-20240523. Looks like org_9f3b didn't get the new entitlement toggled correctly; the feature-entitlements table shows null for "new_ui_access".

jenni (customer): So the UI flip on our side triggered the entitlement check and that failed? I assumed entitlement checks were only for server-side feature gating.

maria (eng-platform): Behaviour: the frontend calls our hosted API with the customer's API key; runtime checks whether the account is entitled to use the model/route (some costly models are behind higher tiers). If entitlement service returns false, runtime returns 403. Right now we anonymize the reason for security, which backfires UX-wise.

alex (support): For immediate mitigation: sam, can you manually set new_ui_access=true for org_9f3b so Jenni's customers are unblocked? Then we should add a clearer error payload for entitlement-related 403s (e.g., {"error":"entitlement_error","code":"ENTITLEMENT_PLAN","message":"Requires plan upgrade or feature enablement"}) so support and customers can triage faster.

sam (billing): Manual toggle done — org_9f3b now has new_ui_access=true. Jenni, can you retry?

jenni (customer): Retried at 09:21 UTC — success! Thanks.

maria (eng-platform): Root cause summary: the seat migration job had a path where feature flags weren’t backfilled for certain orgs that had legacy seat metadata. That caused the entitlement check to deny access even though API key was valid. We need two fixes: 1) backfill script + data migration (low risk) 2) change gateway to add an explicit entitlement code in the response header/body for distinguishability.

alex (support): Also we should update our support runbook: when a 403 is reported, check these in order — a) api key prefix and signature b) x-request-id lookup for entitlement response c) billing/feature toggles. Add the sample curl and the exact header to copy.

maria (eng-platform): Proposed API change (short term): add header `x-entitlement-reason: ENTITLEMENT_PLAN` when entitlement check fails. Long term: structured body as Alex suggested and metrics to SLO dashboard.

alex (support): Repro steps for eng: 1) create test org with legacy seats 2) leave new_ui_access unset 3) perform POST -> expect 403 4) inspect feature-entitlements logs: feature-entitlements returned code ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED. We should add an automated unit test in the runtime that asserts the gateway preserves the reason header.

maria (eng-platform): I'll open a small PR to the runtime gateway to preserve entitlement code in `x-entitlement-reason` and to return a descriptive JSON body for entitlement failures. I'll also deploy to canary.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/runtime-gateway v2024.05.23-entitlement-preserve started — canary=1/10 nodes.

alex (support): Thanks. Action items assigned: sam — backfill + migration schedule; maria — PR & canary; eng-sre/watch — monitor canary for errors; support — update runbook and send customer-facing note to Jenni.

jenni (customer): Really appreciate the quick turnaround and the manual fix. Two asks: (1) could you add a clearer error so our client app can show a friendly message vs "invalid API key"? (2) doc a recommended client behavior (e.g., surface 403 entitlement errors differently).

alex (support): Yes — we'll patch the UI error message and add a short note in the API docs about entitlement 403 semantics and the recommended client UX. Closing once migration/backfill and gateway fix are in prod. :thumbsup:
